text:
maria: Hey team — quick coord on docs PR #842: adding updated function/tool-calling examples and a new section for structured output (JSON schema + guardrails). I hit a couple CI failures and want a sanity review on the SDK snippets before merge. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/842

sanjay: I can take the runtime/response-shape bits. Which SDK snippets are failing?

maria: The Python example for tool invocation and the TypeScript structured-output example. CI logged a lint error and an invalid code block in the TS sample. Also the runtime behavior changed and we might need a short migration note.

kim: I saw markdown-lint flagging an unclosed ``` fenced code block in the TS snippet. Also the TS sample was missing an import for parseJson helper. I can push a fix to the branch.

alex: FYI runtime changed how we return tool calls: previously we returned top-level `function_call`, now it's nested under `response.actions.tool_call`. Docs need a migration note under "Migration guide -> function calling" to avoid users breaking.

linda: Can someone paste an example of the new response shape? I'll write the migration blurb once I have exact fields.

sanjay: Example (new shape):
```json
{
  "id": "resp_01",
  "response": {
    "text": "Invoking tool...",
    "actions": [{
      "type": "tool_call",
      "tool_name": "search",
      "tool_args": { "q": "redwood inference" }
    }]
  }
}
```
Old shape for reference:
```json
{
  "id": "resp_01",
  "text": "Invoking tool...",
  "function_call": {
    "name": "search",
    "arguments": { "q": "redwood inference" }
  }
}
```
sanjay: Also recommend the docs show how to use the SDK helper `parseJson` so people don't rely on brittle string parsing. Example snippet (Python):
```py
from redwood import Client, parse_json
client = Client()
resp = client.generate(...)
call = parse_json(resp.response, path="response.actions[0].tool_args")
```

ci-bot: CI check failed — markdownlint: MD046/fenced-code-blocks; line 78. docs/tests/snippets/test_ts_snippets.py: example import error.

kim: pushed fix: added missing import and closed fence. Also swapped the TS snippet to use `parseJson` from `@redwood/inference-sdk` and updated example to the new response path.

alex: I'll run the link-checker to fix a broken anchor. There's an internal link pointing to `/docs/outputs#schema-parsing` that 404s. The new anchor should be `/docs/structured-output#schema-parsing`.

maria: Great. Two more asks: 1) add a short sentence in the structured output section explaining guardrails vs schema validation (guardrails are best-effort; schema is strict). 2) add a tiny snippet showing how to combine guardrails with a lenient schema so users can fail soft.

linda: I'll do the copy pass and add the guardrails wording. Quick draft for the "fail-soft" example:
```json
"guardrails": {
  "mode": "warn",
  "schema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "title": { "type": "string" } } }
}
```

maria: CI rerun queued. If green I'll merge. Anyone want to do a final read for clarity?

kim: quick nit: change `tool_args` -> `args` in Python example to match SDK naming. Pushing patch.

sanjay: I updated the runtime PR to keep compatibility by adding a helper `compatToolCall()` that maps old `function_call` into new `response.actions` shape for 2 releases. We'll mention that in migration note.

ci-bot: All checks passed ✅ — markdownlint, snippets tests, link-check. (run: 1771237942)

maria: Merged PR #842. Thanks everyone :tada: — will follow up with a short release note in #eng-releases to call out the response shape change.

linda: I'll add the release-note blurb and a small example in the changelog.

alex: Good catch on the anchor. I created a tiny script to scan for other `/docs/outputs` anchors that might be stale.

maria: Awesome — closing the loop. If anyone notices docs examples still referencing `function_call` please ping me and I'll do a quick sweep. :pray:
